title: edge-deploy-choreography-checklist-and-blocker-catalog-jun-2026
content:
Purpose:
Quick working note capturing choreography steps, small checklist updates, and a living catalog of active customer blockers for VPC / on-prem edge installs. This is intentionally informal — use as the canonical short-hand for on-call huddles and weeklies until we fold verified items into the install runbook.

Summary (tl;dr):
- Most installs progressing: 4 active customers in staging, 2 in day-0, 1 in day-2 remediation.
- Highest-impact blocker: AtlasCorp private network MTU+GRE tunneling causing KV cache reconnects (PD-4321).
- Short-term ops: temporary circuit breaker flag + route pinning deployed to Canary nodes; monitoring alert thresholds lowered for 48h.

This week highlights:
- Canary rollout of route-pin-fallback (release PR #2152) to reduce cross-node KV fetches. Observed 30% fewer reconnects in internal sim.
- New onboarding checklist item 7.b added: confirm customer-side NAT/PAT mapping for outbound ephemeral ports (saves mysterious egress failures).
- Ran two daylight installs (BlueRiver, AtlasCorp) with new preflight nav checks; BlueRiver cleared day-0 in 4 hours, AtlasCorp stalled on MTU/GRE.

Active customer threads (short):
- AtlasCorp (customer alias): PD-4321 — symptoms: intermittent model-state resyncs when >6 concurrent streams, correlated with GRE fragmentation on customer WAN. Temporary mitigation: forced small-MSS on edge side + disable jumbo frames in overlay. Longer fix: coordinate with network team and customer infra to align MTU across transit path. Next step: Diego to own packet capture handoff (ETA 2026-06-17).
- BlueRiver: successful day-0; minor auth header mismatch due to proxy rewrite rules. Action: Chloe to push auth header passthrough docupdate and a one-liner fix in agent (PR 2189).
- NorthPark Analytics: day-2 perf regression (high latency spikes) after model bundle swap. Likely RC: node-level CPU steal from backup cron. Samir to correlate cron schedule with rollout times and propose stagger (ETA 2026-06-18).

Blocker catalog (ranked):
1) PD-4321 (AtlasCorp) — Network fragmentation + GRE resulting in KV cache reconnects and partial sequence loss. Severity: P1 for customer SLA. Dependencies: Network-eng, customer-NOC. Mitigation: route-pin-fallback and MSS clamp deployed.
2) PD-4337 — Onprem installer fails on systems with non-standard NSS libs (observed in two enterprise sites). Symptoms: installer aborts at docker-init with cryptic libc mismatch. Mitigation: vendor shim in staging; longer term wrap: build static bootstrap binary.
3) RWINF-6789 — Disk inode exhaustion on older onprem nodes after rotated logs not cleaned. Low frequency but high impact when it hits. Task: small housekeeping cron and disk-pressure alert.

Runbook / checklist updates (temporary):
- Preflight checklist additions (add numbered items to /runbooks/onprem-preflight.md):
  * Confirm upstream MTU path (ask customer for traceroute + ping -s tests).
  * Validate overlay GRE handling on customer edge device (vendor/firmware).
  * Verify outbound ephemeral port range + NAT mapping.
  * Confirm time sync across host and edge gateway (ntp/chrony drift will cause cert handshake timeouts).
- Day-0 ops: include step to wrap agent logs with trace-id->request-id crosswalk for first 24 hours. Saves a 2hr debug loop we hit yesterday.

Operational notes / heuristics learned:
- When customers report "random disconnects" with high concurrency, first suspect is MTU/GRE/Jumbo interplay rather than model runtime. Packet captures are high-ROI and should be requested up-front.
- Small-MSS clamp buys enough headroom to stabilize KV reconnect behavior while we coordinate longer fixes with customer network.
- Canary rollout: prefer route-pin-fallback only on 10% of nodes for 6h windows, then expand based on reconnection delta.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we add static bootstrap binary to ship artifacts? Pros: fewer installer failures in heterogenous environments. Cons: larger artifact, more build/QA surface. Proposal: Samir to prototype static boot and present perf/security implications (ETA 2026-06-21).
- SLA escalation thresholds: should we auto-open a SE engagement for any P1 that persists beyond 4 business hours? Current manual. Need agreement from CS.

Action items (owner -> what -> ETA):
- Diego Mendez -> collect packet captures from AtlasCorp + upload to PD-4321 thread -> 2026-06-17
- Chloe Hart -> patch auth header passthrough + update preflight doc -> PR 2189 -> 2026-06-16
- Samir Patel -> prototype static bootstrap binary & report feasibility -> 2026-06-21
- Priya Singh -> create disk-pressure alert playbook and mitigation cron -> 2026-06-18
- Aisha Coleman (me) -> consolidate checklist into runbook and publish draft on Confluence -> 2026-06-16

Notes to self / meeting prep bullets for Friday ops huddle:
- Bring packet capture from AtlasCorp and show MSS/clamp before/after graphs.
- Quick demo of route-pin-fallback telemetry.
- Agree on SE auto-engage SLA threshold for persistent P1s.

References / links (working):
- PD-4321 JIRA thread: https://rwinf.atlassian.net/browse/PD-4321
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.rwinf.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=987654321
- Slack channel: #install-atlascorp (pinned: tcpdump-collection.txt)
- PR for fallback: https://github.com/rwinf/edge-agent/pull/2152

Appendix (raw notes / scratch):
- observed: FRAG_OK counters high on gateway (customer reported jumbo frames) -> got connection drops when >6 streams
- hack: forced tcp_mss = 1200 in agent kernel space; seemed stable in sim but need customer approval
- unsorted TODOs: check rpm vs apt differences for installer shim; add installer verbose mode flag; collect telemetry around DNS timeouts during day-2

If anything needs to be split into separate trackers, call it out in the Friday huddle. This doc is intentionally ephemeral — I'll prune and merge the final runbook changes after sign-off.
